description:
Decouple stream-chunk arrival from rendering. Per-chunk handlers in `OctoPi.TUI.Interactive` become near-no-ops; rendering is driven by a tick. This is the structural change `.4` and `.5` build on top of — both store their state inside the pending-render container introduced here.

## Why

`Interactive`'s mailbox FIFO-orders `:hid_event` (keystrokes) and `:octo_pi_agent_event` (stream chunks). Today, each `OctoPi.Agent.Event.MessageUpdate` triggers a synchronous full-transcript render including Earmark lex + syntax highlight + ANSI wrap of the entire growing assistant message. Keypresses queue behind that work. By moving the render off the chunk path and onto a tick, multiple chunks coalesce into a single render and key handlers run between ticks.

Confirm head-of-line correlation with `.2`'s baseline before starting.

## Code references

- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex:520-524` — the `:octo_pi_agent_event` `handle_info` clause to no-op.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex:1536-1537` — `update_transcript` for `OctoPi.Agent.Event.MessageUpdate`; current synchronous render entry point.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex:655, :896-911` — `send_render`/`build_screen`; the work being deferred.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex:1539, :1557` — `MessageEnd` event handlers; this is the **stream-close** signal that triggers force-flush.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/render_loop.ex:34-80` — the idle/deadline/drain pattern to mirror. Key idea: arm a deadline on first event since last tick, drain the mailbox on the deadline, fire one render, return to idle.
- Project memory: prefer `{:noreply, state, ms}` GenServer timeout returns over `Process.send_after/3`.

## Shape

Per-chunk path:

1. `MessageUpdate` arrives. Append the delta into a `pending_partial` field on `Interactive`'s state.
2. If no tick is currently scheduled, return `{:noreply, state, tick_ms}` to arm a GenServer timeout.
3. Otherwise just return `{:noreply, state}` — the existing pending tick will pick up this delta.

Per-tick path (`handle_info(:timeout, _)` or equivalent):

1. Materialize the partial assistant message from `pending_partial` (in v1, by passing the accumulated text through the existing `Markdown` renderer; `.5` will replace this step with incremental lex).
2. Run the existing `render_transcript` / `send_render` flow.
3. Clear `pending_partial`.

Stream-close path: when `MessageEnd` arrives, force-flush the pending partial *before* processing the finalize. Don't wait for the tick — the user expects the final form immediately.

Non-text events (tool-call boundaries, `MessageEnd`, etc.) MUST stay ordered with deltas. Either route them through the same pending-state machinery (so they fire after a flush of any pending deltas) or flush before handling them. Reordering produces visible glitches.

## Tick budget

`RenderLoop` uses 16 ms but only does diff+write. This tick does Markdown work and is heavier; start at 33 ms (≈ 30 fps). Confirm against telemetry from `.1` after the change — the goal is `transcript.render` p99 < tick.

## Acceptance

- `MessageUpdate` `handle_info` p99 (telemetry from `.1`) drops to sub-millisecond regardless of message length.
- `transcript.render` call rate during streaming is bounded by tick rate, not chunk rate.
- `key.latency` p99 during a long streaming response improves materially vs `.2`'s baseline (ideally back to non-streaming p99 levels).
- Streaming stays visually smooth in tmux — deltas appear at perceived real-time pace, not in 1-second jolts.
- `MessageEnd` produces an immediate visible final render with no perceptible delay.
- Existing `apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/interactive_test.exs` and `interactive_integration_test.exs` continue to pass; add tests for the coalescing behavior (multiple `MessageUpdate`s within `tick_ms` produce one render) and stream-close force-flush.

## Tests

Per project memory: no `Process.sleep` for synchronization in tests. Drive timing assertions via telemetry handlers attached to the new spans, or via injectable clock / tick. The existing test files use a `VirtualTerminal` (`apps/octo_pi_tui/test/support/virtual_terminal.ex`) — extend that pattern.
title: Pull-tick render coalescing in Interactive
